statement: DAF sponsors may use Rev. Proc. 2017-53 guidelines for the §4966(c)(2)(A) exception until further guidance; written advice from a qualified tax practitioner (attorney, CPA, EA) is current while law is unchanged and facts are from the grantee's current or prior taxable year (up to ~2 years); public-support advice current for two taxable years after the test period.
counsel_question: May advice procured by another grantor be relied on?

statement: REG-142338-07 remains proposed as of 2026-11-23: Federal Register API shows no final or withdrawal document after the 2024-04-19 hearing notice; a Council on Foundations page (2026-05-08) says not finalized. If finalized, the proposal would codify ED for DAFs and treat foreign governments as §170(b)(1)(A) organizations for exclusively public purposes.
counsel_question: Applicability date and transition when final.

statement: Sponsoring organizations may continue to rely on Notice 2006-109 §3 grantor reliance standards, as modified, until further guidance (Notice 2014-4 §3.02).
applies_to_activity: grants to Type I/II/FI-III supporting organizations
counsel_question: Certification form wording.

topic: Trump account general funding contributions via DAF
statement: A DAF distribution funding a §530A general funding contribution furthers 501(c)(3) purposes, is a §170(c)(2)(B) expenditure, is not a §4966 distribution to a natural person, and is treated as satisfying ER; applies to taxable years beginning on/after 2026-01-01; expires 2029-09-30.
counsel_question: §4967 where the class includes the donor's family?

topic: Form 990 Schedules I and F grant reporting
statement: Grantmaking public charities report grants over $5,000 per domestic recipient on Schedule I and foreign grants/activities (region, purpose, manner of disbursement, ED/ER procedures) on Schedule F.
citation: IRC §6033; Form 990 Schedules I and F instructions (not re-read)
counsel_question: Current-year line mapping (CPA).

statement: 'Domestic concern' includes any corporation, association or unincorporated organization organized under US state law, which on its face includes nonprofit corporations; payments benefiting foreign officials to obtain business are prohibited.
counsel_question: Does a charitable grant 'obtain or retain business'? Diligence standard?

statement: Financial institutions under FTC jurisdiction must notify the FTC within 30 days of discovering a notification event affecting 500+ consumers (16 CFR 314.4(j), effective 2024-05-13). FTC jurisdiction generally excludes bona fide nonprofits; it may reach a for-profit operator only if the operator is itself a financial institution (not merely a service provider).
counsel_question: Is the operator a 'financial institution' or only a service provider?

topic: Money transmission / MSB status of platform operator
statement: An operator that receives and transmits charitable funds in its own name may be a money transmitter under state law and an MSB under 31 CFR 1010.100(ff)(5); the payment-processor exemption is framed around payments for goods or services via BSA-regulated clearing systems, which a grant is not. Sponsor-titled accounts with instruction-only authority are the main mitigating design.
counsel_question: Multistate analysis of instruction-only model.

topic: Investment adviser status of platform operator
statement: A for-profit operator that provides advice about securities (model portfolios, allocation recommendations) for compensation may be an investment adviser (federal or state); Advisers Act §203(b)(4) exempts charitable organizations, not their vendors.
counsel_question: Does executing sponsor-selected models without advice avoid status?

statement: Receiving transaction-based compensation for effecting securities transactions (e.g. liquidating contributed securities) can require broker-dealer registration; Exchange Act §3(e) charitable exclusion is for the charity.
counsel_question: Fee structures that avoid transaction-based compensation.

statement: Commercial email from any sender (including nonprofits) needs sender ID, opt-out honoured within 10 business days; transactional/relationship messages largely exempt.
counsel_question: Classify fundraising appeals sent by sponsor to donors.

statement: Autodialed/prerecorded calls and texts to wireless numbers require prior express consent (written for telemarketing); tax-exempt nonprofit exemptions relate to telephone solicitation rules; consent revocation by reasonable means.
counsel_question: Status of FCC revocation-rule provisions in 2026.

statement: No DOJ Title III web regulation (general knowledge); DOJ 2024 Title II rule (WCAG 2.1 AA) binds state/local governments only; private-sector exposure is case law and state law (e.g. Unruh). WCAG 2.2 AA is industry practice.
citation: ADA Title III; 28 CFR Part 35 (Title II)
counsel_question: Exposure for white-label sponsor sites.

statement: Tax-exempt holders are generally not exempt; priority to state of payee's last known address, then holder's state of incorporation (Texas v. New Jersey, 1965, general knowledge); some states exempt business-to-business property.
citation: State UPA/RUUPA; Texas v. New Jersey, 379 U.S. 674
counsel_question: B2B exemption applicability to charity payees.

topic: State charity registry standing of grantees
statement: California prohibits delinquent/suspended/revoked organizations from operating or soliciting in CA; this binds the grantee, not the grantor.
citation: Cal. Gov. Code §12585 et seq.; 11 CCR §312 (not read)
counsel_question: None (policy signal only).

statement: Exemption is automatically revoked after three consecutive years of non-filing (§6033(j)); reinstatement can be retroactive if applied within 15 months (Rev. Proc. 2014-11), so held grants may become releasable.
counsel_question: Is a grant made during the gap covered by retroactive reinstatement for §4966?

statement: December 2022 rules added humanitarian and NGO general licenses across many sanctions programs; activity outside a license remains prohibited and must be documented.
counsel_question: Which GLs apply to DAF grants?

statement: ER requires a written commitment signed by a grantee officer (repay unused funds, annual reports, records, no lobbying/electioneering), annual grantee reports while funds unspent, and grantee records kept 4 years after use.
counsel_question: DAF-specific modifications under NPRM.

statement: E-SIGN §7001(c) consumer-consent disclosures apply to consumers, not to organizations; electronic grant agreements with charities need no consumer disclosures.
counsel_question: Confirm for unincorporated associations.

statement: SB 26-189 (signed 2026-05-14) effective 2027-01-01 covers ADMT materially influencing consequential decisions (employment, housing, lending, insurance, health care, education, essential government services); charitable grant decisions are not listed.
counsel_question: Does any donor-account decision fall within 'financial or lending'?
